title: Elasticity roadmap charter — Q2 planning for reserved pools & autoscale
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Define a focused Q2 roadmap and execution charter to improve Dedicated capacity elasticity: reduce cold-start time for reserved GPU pools, enable fast safe bursts, and tighten autoscale guardrails so we can meet latency SLOs while reducing overprovisioned spend.

Scope: This charter covers the cross-functional work required across product, runtime engineering, and SRE for Dedicated: 1) Prewarm and reservoir strategies (predictive warm pools + fastpath burst lanes). 2) Autoscale policy taxonomy and canary criteria (safety thresholds, rollback windows). 3) Observability hooks (per-route token cost, prewarm effectiveness, burst success rate). 4) Ops playbook for capacity incidents and controlled rollouts to customers.

Deliverables by due date:
- Finalized roadmap with milestones and owners.
- Canary criteria and abort conditions doc.
- Autoscale policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive).
- Runbook for oncall and capacity incidents; playbook for customer-facing degradations.
- Experiment matrix and success metrics for pilot customers.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in median cold-start latency for reserved pools (for targeted burst scenarios).
- <5% failed burst attempts across pilot customers in first 30 days.
- 10% reduction in overall committed-reservation cost for participating pools without adverse SLO regressions.

Out-of-scope: wholesale re-architecture of serving runtime kernels or new quantization profiles; separate initiative will handle kernel-level optimization.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive autoscale policies may cause overspend. Mitigation: tiered launch with telemetry-backed thresholds and daily budget caps.
- Risk: customer-facing regressions during canaries. Mitigation: pre-signed fallback routes and automatic rollback + customer communication template.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Align stakeholders and owners for each deliverable.
2) Validate metrics and available telemetry with Observability team.
3) Create experiment cohorts and target pilot customers (2–4 customers).
4) Draft canary/rollback templates and get legal/CS sign-off for customer outreach.
